decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presentation linked the initial spec; the client reports its save form required a manually entered title. Round 1 client: "I have to enter the title (and it's required). That's not what I want... I mostly just paste and save."
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client replaced the title-required save flow with the reference-conforming URL-only flow.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker summary: "Deferred: ... automatic page metadata." Round 1 client: "I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title, description, and its little icon for me automatically... I'd really like it in."
decisions.note: At the specification gate, automatic metadata was explicitly deferred and the client requested the missing capability. The response did not mention the reference's preview-image field, which becomes observable in the revised decision below.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope includes "editing." Round 1 client says editing is "the right shape" and adds that collected text should remain changeable afterward.
decisions.note: The presented ability to edit bookmark information conforms at the initial specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope includes "deletion." Round 1 client approves "deleting with a confirmation" as "the right shape."
decisions.note: Deletion is a conforming initial-specification decision; confirmation is an additional safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presentation's linked spec allowed duplicate creation, as identified in the review. Round 1 client: "Your version lets me deliberately keep a second copy. I don't want duplicates at all... take me to the existing one to edit."
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client supplied the reference-conforming duplicate-save behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope includes "tags." Round 1 client lists tags among the parts that are "all the right shape."
decisions.note: Tag assignment is a recorded conforming initial-specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client describes the presented filter as supporting "one" tag and asks additionally for more than one tag at a time.
decisions.note: Filtering by one selected tag already conforms to REF-BM-11. The requested multi-tag enhancement is not itself a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope includes "search." Round 1 client: "Plain text search is good."
decisions.note: The recorded basic full-text-search decision is conforming; the transcript does not present a separable decision about case sensitivity or field coverage.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation offered plain search without tag-query syntax. Round 1 client: "I also want to search by a tag specifically (something like typing `#news`)."
decisions.note: The client requested the missing #tag search behavior at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation offered plain search rather than structured Boolean search. Round 1 client asks to "combine terms — this AND that, or one OR the other."
decisions.note: The client surfaced and corrected the absence of Boolean search, although the response itself named AND and OR rather than the reference's entire grammar.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation offered plain search without exact-phrase syntax. Round 1 client requests "search an exact phrase in quotes."
decisions.note: The client requested the missing quoted-phrase behavior at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's stated scope includes favorites but no unread status. Round 1 client: "separately I want to mark a link as something I still need to read."
decisions.note: The client requested the missing Read Later/unread state.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker's stated scope omits an unread perspective. Round 1 client requests being able "to pull up just those unread ones on their own."
decisions.note: The client requested the missing separate unread view.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 presentation has no read-state transition. Round 1 client: "Marking it as read would take it off that list."
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing mark-read behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client identifies the presented decision: "You've got bulk actions as out of scope." The client requests selecting "a bunch of links" and tagging or archiving them together.
decisions.note: The client requested bulk actions over an explicit selection.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client identifies bulk actions as out of scope and requests acting on "everything currently showing after I've searched or filtered."
decisions.note: The client requested whole-result bulk operations scoped by the active filter.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope includes "sorting." Round 1 client lists sorting among the features that are "all the right shape."
decisions.note: Sorting is a conforming initial-specification decision.

decisions.evidence: The Round 1 scope does not include notes. Round 1 client requests "writing a note in a link with basic formatting that shows nicely when I look at it" and asks that it be brought into the revision.
decisions.note: Although described as less urgent, the client expressly requested the missing formatted-note behavior rather than accepting its omission.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker scope includes "archiving." Round 1 client says archiving is "the right shape."
decisions.note: Archiving is a conforming initial-specification decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents archiving and deletion as separate scope items. The client approves both; Round 5 maker later expressly describes "permanent deletion."
decisions.note: The presented distinction between reversible archiving and deletion conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: The Round 1 scope lacks saved filters. Round 1 client requests "saving a search-plus-tags combination so I can reuse it later" and asks that it be included in the revision.
decisions.note: The client requested the missing reusable bundle/saved-view behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly says "Deferred: ... import/export." Round 5 client identifies import as desired but accepts the departure: "at some point I'd love a way to bring in bookmarks I've already got saved elsewhere... That's a future wish, not something I need before saying yes."
decisions.note: The original import deferral receives an explicit eventual disposition at implementation review. This is counted once as an accepted divergence, not as an earlier unexpressed divergence plus a later one.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly says "Deferred: ... import/export." Round 5 client identifies export as desired but accepts the departure: "and to get mine back out. That's a future wish, not something I need before saying yes."
decisions.note: The client explicitly states the export expectation and accepts its deferral during final review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents automatic retrieval after entering an address. Round 2 client approves "pasting an address" and having its details arrive automatically.
decisions.note: The revised URL-only save decision conforms at the revised-specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker's revised metadata decision expressly enumerates "Automatic title, description, and site-icon retrieval" but not the reference-required preview image. Round 2 client repeats those same three fields and approves without identifying the missing preview image.
decisions.note: The revised specification remains incomplete for REF-BM-02. The approval does not demonstrate awareness of the omitted preview-image requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says the revised spec has captured the requested automatic metadata workflow. Round 2 client confirms the fetched details and says everything requested was picked up, following the Round 1 requirement that the text remain editable.
decisions.note: The revised metadata-editing decision conforms at the revised-specification stage.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: "Separate Read Later status" and "New bookmarks default to read unless explicitly marked Read Later." Round 2 client approves the separate Read Later behavior.
decisions.note: The revised specification now supports explicitly marking a bookmark unread.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents a separate Read Later "view." Round 2 client praises "the separate Read Later list."
decisions.note: The revised specification's separate unread list conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says the revised spec captures the requested Read Later behavior; Round 2 client says it has "picked up everything I asked about," including the earlier mark-read removal rule.
decisions.note: The revised read-state transition is accepted as conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents "Bulk actions across selected bookmarks." Round 2 client approves being able to select a batch and act on it.
decisions.note: The revised selected-bookmark bulk-action decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents bulk actions over "the complete filtered result set." Round 2 client approves acting on "a whole filtered batch."
decisions.note: The revised filtered-collection bulk-action decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents advanced search with "`#tags`." Round 2 client specifically approves searching by `#tag`.
decisions.note: The revised tag-query syntax conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents "quoted phrases." Round 2 client approves "exact phrases in quotes."
decisions.note: The revised exact-phrase search decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker expressly enumerates advanced search with "`AND`, `OR`" and multi-tag filters, omitting the reference-required `NOT` operator and parenthesized groups. Round 2 client repeats AND/OR and approves without identifying those missing grammar elements.
decisions.note: At the revised-specification gate, structured search remains incomplete. The client's approval does not qualify as an accepted divergence because the client never states the missing NOT/parentheses expectation or difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents "Strict normalized-address duplicate prevention, opening the existing bookmark in edit mode." Round 2 client approves the app taking them to the existing bookmark "instead of ever making a duplicate."
decisions.note: The revised duplicate-save behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents "Basic formatted notes." Round 2 client recognizes these as the requested formatted notes and approves them.
decisions.note: The revised formatted-note decision is functionally conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker presents "Reusable named saved views." Round 2 client identifies them as the requested reusable saved searches and approves them after having specified a search-plus-tags combination in Round 1.
decisions.note: The revised saved-view/bundle decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 client asks whether an archived unread bookmark disappears from Read Later while archived and returns there after restoration, saying "that's exactly what I'd want." Round 3 maker answers: "Yes—the approved archive/Read Later behavior is preserved exactly," and the Round 3 client approves the plan.
decisions.note: The clarification is linked to its eventual confirmation and counted once. It resolves as a conforming archive/Read Later interaction, not an unresolved decision.

decisions.evidence: Round 5 maker presents the completed Read Later/archive behavior. Round 5 client reports that "Read Later list and Archive" exist "as their own separate places" and approves the application.
decisions.note: The implementation-review decision to expose a separate archive list conforms.
